Patron saint of Piombino: Saint Anastasia, feast 8 May. Her cult in the town is attested from the fourteenth century, and in 1471 the Council of Elders decreed an annual palio for her feast (diocesan records; the canonical recognition of 1874 formalized an existing cult). Saint Cerbonius, often cited instead, is the patron of the diocese of Massa Marittima, successor of the see of Populonia, and of Populonia itself, not of the town of Piombino. The distinction matters here because the very council that shared power with the Appiani, the constitutional feature Leonardo's employers dealt with, was the body administering the patronal feast

background.text: Patron saint: Saint Anastasia (feast 8 May) . Her cult in the town is attested from the fourteenth century; in 1471 the Council of Elders (Consiglio degli Anziani) decreed an annual palio for her feast, which continued through the sixteenth century B . Saint Cerbonius, sometimes cited in this connection, is the patron of the diocese of Massa Marittima, heir of the see of Populonia, not of the town: see the notes on contested points D
Government: A dual regime: the Appiani as lords in coordination with the communal Council of Elders. Cesare Borgia held the town from 1501 to 1503; Jacopo IV was restored in 1503
Terrain and water: A harbor town on a promontory into the Tyrrhenian Sea, facing Elba, whose iron ore was the core of the state's value
Economy and trade: Shipment of Elban iron ore and coastal trade, absorbing part of the commercial sphere of declining Pisa
